target.title: fix: treat EPERM as alive in isPidAlive
target.body:
Related: #105696

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where a live process that returns `EPERM` from `process.kill(pid, 0)` was treated as not alive by `isPidAlive`, while `isPidDefinitelyDead` correctly treats `EPERM` as not definitely dead. That mismatch can make lock/owner liveness look dead for a process that still exists.

## Why This Change Was Made
Align `isPidAlive` with `isPidDefinitelyDead` for the `EPERM` case: if the kernel says permission denied for signal 0, the PID still refers to a live process. This is not a speculative `tasklist` Windows path. On current Node (v24.15.0 win32) `process.kill(pid, 0)` already works for self/live PIDs and returns `ESRCH` for missing PIDs; the remaining helper bug was the `EPERM` swallow.

## User Impact
Owners and claim locks that hit permission-restricted PIDs via the shared helpers are less likely to be treated as dead and stolen. No change for normal self-PID checks.

## Callers and Telegram / EINVAL note
Shared `isPidAlive` callers on this branch (import from `src/shared/pid-alive.ts`):
- `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts` (`resolveGatewayOwnerStatus`)
- `src/agents/session-write-lock.ts` (`inspectLockPayload`)

Related but separate local helpers (not this PR's export):
- `src/channels/message/ingress-claim-owner.ts` `processExists` (Telegram / channel ingress claim liveness via `isIngressClaimOwnedByOtherLiveProcess`). It already treats non-`ESRCH`/non-`EINVAL` errors as alive, so `EPERM` is already alive there. Current `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.ts` no longer embeds its own `processExists`; claim ownership goes through that shared ingress claim helper.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts` has its own `processExists` that already returns true on `EPERM`.
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts` and `src/test-utils/process-tree.ts` define local namesakes.

About #105696's EINVAL/ENOSYS claim: on Node v24.15.0 win32, a full `tasklist` PID scan of `process.kill(pid, 0)` observed only `OK`, `EPERM`, and `ESRCH` (no `EINVAL`, no `ENOSYS`). Signal 0 is usable on this Node/Windows combination. So the linked report's "signal 0 always fails with EINVAL/ENOSYS on Windows" premise does not match current HEAD runtime. This PR still fixes a real shared-helper mismatch for `EPERM`; it does not claim to be the sole Telegram spool fix, because Telegram claim liveness does not call shared `isPidAlive`.

## Evidence
After-fix real EPERM branch (win32, Node v24.15.0). Restricted PID is Windows `System` (PID 4). Process name only; no tokens/hosts.

Raw `process.kill` probe:

```
node v24.15.0 platform win32
raw_self {"code":null,"ok":true}
raw_missing {"code":"ESRCH","ok":false,"errno":-4040}
raw_eperm_pid 4 {"code":"EPERM","ok":false,"errno":-4048}
```

Loaded `src/shared/pid-alive.ts` helpers after the fix:

```
isPidAlive_self true
isPidAlive_missing false
isPidAlive_eperm true
isPidDefinitelyDead_eperm false
isPidDefinitelyDead_missing true
parity_eperm_alive_not_dead true
```

Before-fix inline comparison (old swallow: any kill error => not alive):

```
OLD_eperm_pid4 false
```

Tasklist scan histogram (same host, same Node):

```
{"n":535,"hist":{"OK":348,"EPERM":184,"ESRCH":3},"node":"v24.15.0","platform":"win32"}
```

Focused tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts src/shared/pid-alive.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

## AI assistance
This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Cursor/Grok). Human author: Stan Shih (@stantheman0128). Please review carefully.

target.title: fix: beta releases require manual reruns after plugin publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The 2026.7.2 beta release path took many hours because independent validation, platform, npm, and plugin-registry work was repeatedly serialized or rerun. A beta could remain blocked on plugin ecosystem convergence even after the core release was already safe to publish.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Freezes a product-complete Code SHA and reuses its validation evidence instead of revalidating moving metadata.
- Runs independent release readiness and cross-OS work concurrently with explicit caps, caching, timing, and resumable evidence.
- Classifies evidence impact so docs/workflow metadata does not invalidate product proof.
- Makes beta verification report live, degraded, or failed states without treating small plugin-registry lag as a core beta blocker.
- Publishes prerelease core first, then moves plugin npm to ClawHub convergence into a detached trusted continuation. Stable releases, explicit wait mode, and plugin-only releases remain blocking.
- Keeps the detached path safe: immutable parent-bound handoff, authenticated child identity artifacts, attempt-bound retry deduplication, cancellation cleanup, ambiguous-dispatch reconciliation, terminal repair, and always-uploaded evidence.
- Uses GitHub's supported `return_run_details` workflow-dispatch response to bind run IDs immediately; ambiguous responses still fail closed and reconcile by authenticated correlation. Contract: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-19-workflow-dispatch-api-now-returns-run-ids/

## User Impact

Expected beta critical path: roughly 15–30 minutes plus platform publish variability, instead of waiting for the entire plugin ecosystem. Plugin convergence continues asynchronously and remains visible/repairable. Stable release confidence is unchanged: required ecosystem work still blocks.

No release was created by this optimization work. `2026.7.2-beta.3` predates these final pipeline changes.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `9d2f5d4dbb639ecfcb95b6f5772895534f687691`
- Current head: `a7c66c2992bf12c09c74856a453e8300711e6163`
- Release-focused suite: 516/516 passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29678303536
- Current-head continuation contract: 95/95 passed on Testbox `tbx_01kxwz6ck898q6ksgdx16gmhe2`
- Current-head scoped changed gate: green in 1m29 on the same Testbox; formatting, declarations, test-root typecheck, and script lint all passed
- Whole-branch changed gate: green in 7m40 on a warm exact checkout; SDK surface/baseline, boundaries, typecheck, lint, and import-cycle checks passed
- Full `actionlint` stopped hanging after disabling its already-ignored ShellCheck integration; structural workflow lint now completes locally in under one second
- Workflow-sanity fix: 93/93 focused tests passed on Testbox `tbx_01kxx11355sh49ahy92h45gx0v`; scoped changed gate passed in 1m32
- Embedded Bash syntax checks, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check`: passed
- Mandatory autoreview: clean after iterating through cancellation, retry, artifact-authentication, and run-attempt race findings

Operational timing evidence also confirmed the intended workflow: warm lease reuse avoids repeated 60–100 second hydration/sync costs, while focused workflow tests themselves take about 3.4 seconds.
